content.text: Now the IP chain is express, not inferential: Kubient's warranty at p0033 is a direct non-infringement covenant, which limb (iv) of the indemnity (p0051) converts into a defence-and-indemnity obligation. I'll repair the finding to cite that chain.

input.quote: (i) the Service and any deliverables provided hereunder by Kubient do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party;
input.rationale:
Vendor IP-infringement indemnity IS present, by an express two-part chain rather than a single labelled limb. (1) At p0033 Kubient represents, warrants and covenants that "the Service and any deliverables provided hereunder by Kubient do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party". (2) At p0051 limb (iv), Kubient's indemnity expressly covers "Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement". So a third-party claim that the Service or deliverables infringe IP is a breach of p0033 and is therefore defended and indemnified. Independently, p0047-p0049 make Kubient liable for ALL third-party Claims "arising out of or in connection with" the Services and the Auction Platform, which on its face captures infringement allegations without needing the warranty chain, and p0039-p0040 add IP ownership/licence warranties that feed the same limb (iv). The indemnity is therefore at least as broad as the preferred position's IP limb.

The remaining preferred elements are met: Kubient "agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees" from all third-party Claims including reasonable attorneys' fees (p0047); breach of law is covered via limb (iv) plus the compliance-with-Law warranty (p0041); Vendor-caused data incidents, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are covered by limb (v), the acts or omissions of Kubient or any third party it hires, employs, retains or controls (p0051). Standard procedure is present at p0053-p0055: prompt written notice, indemnitor control of defence and settlement negotiations with no liability-admitting settlement absent the indemnified party's written consent, and cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost and expense - and notice delay does not relieve the indemnifying party, which is pro-AP. The indemnity is also effectively uncapped in our favour: p0027 carves "THE PARTIES' LIABILITY FOR INDEMNIFICATION" out of the consequential-damages exclusion and no cap or super-cap is applied, so the fallback's 3x annual fees ceiling is unnecessary.

Direction is correct on our side: AP's indemnity (p0052) is keyed to its own Content and Properties (including infringement by that Content), unauthorised or inappropriate use, its own breach and its own acts or omissions, with no indemnity running to Kubient in respect of Kubient's Services - so the walk-away scenarios (no Vendor IP indemnity, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services) do not arise.

Two minor sub-elements fall short of ideal preferred wording and are recorded here rather than redlined, per the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements: the Creative limb (p0050) carries a "to the best of its knowledge" qualifier, and AP's indemnity extends slightly beyond Customer-provided content and breach of law to unauthorised use and breach of any representation or warranty. Neither is material to the rule.
